blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A billing job computes totals with `for (int i = 0; i < lines.size(); i++) total += lines.get(i).amount();` over the `List<Line>` it receives. The old CSV parser returned an `ArrayList`; the new one returns a `LinkedList` with the same lines. What happens to the job's running time?

options.text: It stays about the same, since both lists reach an element by its index in constant time
options.says: a LinkedList reaches index i by walking nodes from the nearer end; only ArrayList computes the address

options.text: It stays about the same, since the JIT turns an index loop over a list into an iterator walk
options.says: the loop still calls get(i), and each call starts a new walk; only for-each uses the iterator

options.text: It grows with the square of the line count, since each get(i) walks the nodes from an end
options.says: the loop makes about n squared over four node hops; for-each or an ArrayList keeps it linear

options.text: It grows in step with the line count, since a LinkedList remembers where the last get(i) stopped
options.says: LinkedList keeps no such position; every get(i) walks again from the nearer end

origin.section: A Collection Costs What Its Structure Makes It Cost: ArrayList by Index, ArrayDeque at the Ends

questions.stem: A service builds the tags shown on a product page by adding each tag to a `HashSet<String>` and copying the set into a list. A unit test with 6 tags checks the shown order and passes on every run. In production a product has 30 tags, the test's 6 among them. What can its page show?

options.text: All tags in the order they were added, since the test showed that the set keeps that order
options.says: a hash set promises no order; a small set can look stable until its table grows

options.text: The 6 test tags in the test's order, since a tag's place depends on its hash code alone
options.says: the place also depends on the table size; when the table doubles, the elements are spread again

options.text: The 6 test tags in another order, since a larger table puts the tags in other buckets
options.says: iteration walks the bucket table; past the resize threshold the table doubles and the same tags come out in another order

options.text: All tags in another order on each run, since a HashSet seeds its hashing anew per run
options.says: for the same strings added the same way, a HashSet iterates in the same order every run; it changes with the table size

origin.section: A Hash Set Iterates in Hash Order, and the Order Changes as the Set Grows

questions.stem: A worker calls `poll()` on an `ArrayDeque<String>` each time it is signalled that a job was added, and treats a `null` from `poll()` as the order to stop. To stop it, the shutdown code calls `jobs.add(null)` and then signals. What happens at that `add`?

options.text: It succeeds, and the worker stops at the marker, since the deque stores null like any other element
options.says: ArrayDeque refuses null elements, so the marker is never stored

options.text: It succeeds, and the marker is lost, since the deque skips a null element instead of storing it
options.says: the deque does not skip it silently: add(null) throws NullPointerException

options.text: It throws at once, and the worker never hears the order, since the deque refuses a null element from any method
options.says: ArrayDeque, like ConcurrentHashMap, refuses null so that null from poll means one thing: empty

options.text: It throws at once, and the worker never hears the order, since the deque takes a null element only through offer()
options.says: offer() refuses null too; the difference between add and offer is about capacity, and an ArrayDeque grows as needed

origin.section: ConcurrentHashMap Refuses null, So That null from get Means Absent

questions.stem: Webhooks are kept in a `CopyOnWriteArrayList` and an order event is delivered with a for-each loop over it. While the third of five webhooks is being called, an admin thread removes the fifth. What does the fifth webhook get?

options.text: This order event, since the loop goes over the list as it stood when the loop began
options.says: the remove copies the array; the iterator keeps the one it started with, so the change shows from the next event

options.text: Nothing, since the loop goes over the list as it stands at each step it takes
options.says: the iterator never sees a change made after it began

options.text: Nothing, since the remove makes the loop throw ConcurrentModificationException next
options.says: a CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator never throws it; that is ArrayList's fail-fast iterator

options.text: This order event, since the remove must wait until the loop has gone over the list
options.says: readers hold no lock, so the remove does not wait; it copies the array and swaps it in

origin.section: CopyOnWriteArrayList Copies Its Array on Every Write, So Readers Iterate a Snapshot

concepts: ConcurrentHashMap, the skip-list collections, the concurrent queues and ArrayDeque refuse null, so that null from get or poll means absent or empty without a second call; the copy-on-write classes accept it.
get(i) on a LinkedList walks from the nearer end, so a loop by index over it is quadratic, while an ArrayList reaches any index directly.
